patterns_data.why_it_matters: If the setting and provider mapping are wrong, UM, network, and reimbursement teams cannot target the right business lever.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Validate facility and provider mapping for Not Mapped claims in ME, CA, and GA, then reclassify the claims so site-of-care, contract, and utilization actions can be assigned to the correct teams.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Not Mapped facility values and mixed volume versus unit-cost signals indicate the business pattern may be materially distorted by classification issues.
evidence_summary: ME PPO in Not Mapped added about $1.7M with 162 more claims.
ME HMO in Not Mapped added about $0.7M even with 29 fewer claims, pointing to unit-cost lift.
CA HMO in Not Mapped included a roughly $0.4M major cardiovascular episode.
GA HMO in Not Mapped was small dollars but concentrated in 106 claims from THREE RIVERS DIAGNOSTICS.

patterns_data.why_it_matters: Catastrophic outliers can overwhelm trend and require targeted case management or payment review rather than broad policy changes.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Triage these admissions for catastrophic-case review, confirm transplant and trauma payment accuracy, and separate them from routine hospital trend before setting market actions.

Separate trauma-related admissions added about $0.4M, $0.2M, and $0.2M.
Additional liver, sepsis, and red blood cell disorder cases contributed the remaining increase.
